frontmatter.title: How to use virtual machines

audience: Existing Workshop users who already run container workshops daily and have hit an isolation or nesting wall (harder boundary around an AI agent, or running LXD containers and VMs inside a workshop). Readers still evaluating which confinement to pick are pointed back to containers.
title: How to use virtual machines

note: Pre-existing committed customize-workshops index adopted as the basis; no one has edited it. The draft adds the toctree entry for the new VM how-to.

steps.text: Record the Workshop and LXD versions this procedure is verified against
Query LXD for the disk shift capability that decides whether a VM workshop can carry SDKs
Launch a VM workshop before opting in, capturing the refusal and its opt-in hint
Set the workshop.experimental-vms snap setting and restart the workshop daemon
Create a VM workshop definition with workshop init --vm and show the generated YAML
Confirm the virtual-machine confinement with workshop info
Add an SDK to the definition and refresh, capturing the refusal that SDKs are unavailable for virtual machines
Change the definition to container confinement and refresh, capturing the refusal that confinement changed
Stop and start the VM workshop, confirming the lifecycle operations the page summarizes

command: cd .dogen/staging/use-virtual-machines/scratch && workshop init gatecheck --vm && cat .workshop/gatecheck.yaml && workshop launch gatecheck
output_excerpt:
"gatecheck" workshop created at /home/artem.konev@canonical.com/Documents/workshop-akcano/.dogen/staging/use-virtual-machines/scratch/.workshop/gatecheck.yaml
name: gatecheck
base: ubuntu@24.04
confinement: virtual-machine
error: cannot launch "gatecheck": confinement "virtual-machine" is experimental
To opt in: "sudo snap set workshop workshop.experimental-vms=1 && sudo snap restart workshop.workshopd"
reason: The non-zero exit is the outcome under test: launching a virtual-machine workshop without the experimental setting must be refused, and the refusal text with its opt-in hint is what the page documents. The plan did not say how this step obtains a VM definition, so the step creates a throwaway one named gatecheck, keeping the name vmdemo free for the init-vm step.

gaps: {'claim': 'The restart is part of the opt-in, not a follow-up you can defer.', 'why': 'The walk ran the set and the restart together, so setting the option without restarting was never observed failing. The claim rests on the refusal text, which names both commands, and on the launch succeeding after both ran.'}

{'claim': 'A virtual machine consumes more memory and disk than a container.', 'why': 'Not measured during the walk. The disk half is corroborated by the LXD image list, where the 24.04 virtual machine image is materially larger than the container image for the same base; the memory half is a general property of virtual machines, not something read at an origin in this repo.'}

{'claim': 'The first launch on a given base downloads a virtual machine image.', 'why': 'The walk launched against an already cached virtual machine image, so the download itself was not observed. The claim rests on GetBase taking confinement as an argument and on the image list holding separate container and virtual-machine images for the same base.'}

{'observation': 'The two refresh refusals print their prefix twice, as in: cannot refresh "<NAME>": cannot refresh "<NAME>": confinement changed ...', 'why': 'The page reproduces the doubled prefix because that is what the command prints. It looks like an error-wrapping defect in the refresh path rather than intended output; if it is fixed, both code blocks on this page need updating.'}

note: Address all three findings. F-1: delete the workshop stop note entirely; workshop stop sets force false for containers and virtual machines alike, so the page states a difference that does not exist. Do not replace it with another speed claim, and leave the warning block stating cost as memory and disk only. If the refresh nuance is worth documenting, it belongs in Limitations as a refresh statement. F-2: replace the self-referential 'so you can follow the rest of this guide either way' with wording that keeps the information and drops the reference to the guide itself. F-3: the intro names 'the cost' before anything says what it is; either name the cost there or reword so the forward reference goes away.
